analysis:
Examined all 12 primary analyses and every replayed source unit. Replay is incomplete: 59 of 65 reviewed source units are omitted, including executable caller and source-gate revisions needed to independently validate the two proposed findings. Those findings therefore remain material review questions, not established vulnerabilities in this integration response.

The release-provider.yml patch passes the lane environment to source verification (HEAD 142–145) and strengthens final archived-app verification with an Apple/team/provider-identifier requirement (829–834). The latter introduces no demonstrated regression. Changelogs and docs/developer/test.md:1048–1059 describe replacing secret-free ad-hoc dev builds with dev-push reusable execution, inherited secrets, Developer ID signing and notarization. This expands the documented signing trust boundary, but documentation and static test assertions do not independently prove credential accessibility or enforcement. No replayed change directly modifies inference encryption, plaintext handling, cache isolation (T-041), billing, serving authorization, or local fan/hold controls.

Remaining review must reconcile .github/workflows/release-dev-branch.yml:103–106 with release-provider.yml checkout and signing execution: can dev-controlled workflow code consume inherited repository credentials or shared Apple credentials despite the master-owned gate? Independently inspect scripts/provider_release_resume/api.py:73–94 and the claimed review prerequisite in docs/operations/provider-release.md:542–546: does the newly admitted dev ancestry have enforced review before credentialed execution? Neither executable scope is replayed. Also confirm resolver confinement, production/staging secret isolation, publication provenance and qualification separation across release-swift.yml and resolve-provider-release.sh. Relevant contracts are A-005, A-011, A-017, T-013, T-054 and TB-011; Developer ID signing must not imply serving permission (T-052/T-056). No production registration bypass is established. This bounded integration does not clear the earlier credential-exposure or review-prerequisite concerns.
